$comment: The source of the design system's token layer. `npm run tokens` generates tokens.css and index.ts from this file; both are committed and CI regenerates into memory to compare (npm run tokens:check). Edit this file, never the two outputs. Each group's `$prefix` is prepended to its keys to form the custom property name — the colour group's prefix is empty because those names are the documented theming seam (AGENTS.md > Theming) and renaming them would break every override in the wild.

color.$comment: The neutral built-in theme. Overriding any of these in a stylesheet loaded after tokens.css is the supported way to recolour the viewer.

status.$comment: Item status (Open/Doing/Done, see src/status.ts). The status dot maps a value to one of these and nothing else does, so a fourth status needs a colour here and a case there.

chart.$comment: vis-timeline's own furniture: the grid behind the bars and the date axis.

lane.$comment: Six group colours, cycled. A border and its matching fill are one pair: buildItems.ts picks the index, and both halves have to move together or a bar gets one group's outline around another's fill.

space.$comment: The spacing scale. Padding, margin and gap take a step from here; a raw px value in one of those three properties is what check-design-system.sh rejects. Geometry that is not spacing (an icon's width, a border) is a size token or a literal, not a step on this scale.

radius.$comment: `xs` is for a row nested inside an `sm` surface — a menu item in a menu. Matching the parent's radius there makes the row look like it is bleeding past the corner.

mark.$comment: The shape of a round mark: avatars, status dots, point items. Set to a small length to square the whole viewer's marks off in one move.

text.$comment: Font sizes. `md` (13px) is the form and control size, `base` (14px) is body copy — controls sit a step below their surroundings throughout.

control.$comment: Interactive-element heights. `md` is the picker trigger, `lg` the close button and the segmented control — they share a line in the detail panel's header, so the two values are what keeps that row level.

iconSize.$comment: Named `icon-size-` rather than `icon-`: the glyph set in icons.css already owns `--icon-<key>`, and a size token colliding with a mask URL fails silently.

avatar.$comment: One person, one monogram (see src/users.ts). `sm` sits on a text line inside a chip or table cell, `md` stands alone in the header.

shadow.$comment: One elevation per kind of thing that leaves the surface: anything anchored to a trigger, the side panel, the sticky header's scroll shadow, a small mark sitting on top of something else, and an item being dragged. `popover` is shared by the menus, the pickers, the autosuggests and the pricing view's own layers — those were three slightly different shadows for one idea.

z.$comment: The stacking order, in one place because it is a single ordering and used to be eight numbers spread over five stylesheets. `arrows` is the dependency overlay inside the chart; `skeleton` must beat vis-timeline's own layers (which reach 10) or the loading placeholder is drawn through; a context menu is the topmost thing on screen.

motion.$comment: Hover and focus feedback is `fast`; anything that appears or moves on its own is `slow`. Both are honoured only outside prefers-reduced-motion.

focus.$comment: One ring for the whole viewer. Editing surfaces are the documented exception: an input tints its border instead, because a 2px ring around every field you touch reads as a frame (see the Input component).
